intro: `ChatGPT` is an AI assistant from OpenAI that you talk to in plain language. You can ask it to write, explain, summarise, brainstorm, translate and help with code, and it answers in a conversation you can keep refining.
It is available in a web browser and as mobile and desktop apps, so you can use the same assistant on different devices.

capabilities.title: Natural conversation
capabilities.text: Ask follow-up questions and refine an answer step by step.

capabilities.title: Writing and editing
capabilities.text: Draft, rewrite and shorten text in the tone you choose.

capabilities.title: Coding help
capabilities.text: Explain code, suggest fixes and write small programs in many languages.

capabilities.title: Files and images
capabilities.text: Upload documents or pictures and ask questions about them.

capabilities.title: Image creation
capabilities.text: Generate images from a written description.

capabilities.title: Current information
capabilities.text: Search the web when an answer needs recent facts.

helps: ChatGPT helps you get started faster. A blank page becomes a first draft, a confusing topic becomes a clear explanation, and a bug becomes a list of likely causes.
Because you can reply to it, you can steer the result: ask for a shorter version, a simpler tone or a different approach.
why: ChatGPT is one of the most widely used AI assistants. It handles many kinds of tasks in one place, so people use it for study, work and hobbies alike.
It also works as a platform. Developers can build the same models into their own apps through an API.

workflows.title: Learn a topic
workflows.text: Ask for an explanation at your level, then request examples and practice questions.

workflows.title: Draft and polish
workflows.text: Write a rough version yourself and ask ChatGPT to improve the structure and tone.

workflows.title: Debug code
workflows.text: Paste the error and the related code, then ask what is going wrong and how to fix it.

workflows.title: Analyse a document
workflows.text: Upload a report or spreadsheet and ask for a summary or key numbers.

beyond.purpose: Saved assistants with their own instructions
Talk to the assistant by speaking
Remember your preferences between chats
Work with spreadsheets and create charts
Keep chats and files for one topic together
Let developers build the models into their own apps

tips: Give context: say who the answer is for and what you want to do with it.
Share an example of the style or format you like.
Ask it to explain its steps when the answer matters.
Check important facts, numbers and quotes before relying on them.
Some features depend on your plan, and they change often, so check the official site for current details.
audience: ChatGPT suits students, writers, developers, marketers and anyone who wants help with everyday thinking and writing tasks.
It is a good first AI assistant to try because you can start with a simple question and learn by using it.

intro: `Claude` is an AI assistant made by Anthropic. It helps with writing, analysis, coding and research, and it is often chosen for working through long documents and for careful, detailed answers.
You can use it in a browser, in mobile and desktop apps, and through an API for your own projects.

capabilities.title: Long documents
capabilities.text: Read and summarise long reports, contracts and papers in one go.

capabilities.title: Writing and editing
capabilities.text: Draft, revise and adjust tone while keeping your meaning.

capabilities.title: Coding
capabilities.text: Write, review and explain code across many languages.

capabilities.title: Files and images
capabilities.text: Work with PDFs, screenshots and other uploads.

capabilities.title: Artifacts
capabilities.text: See documents, code and small web pages in a side window while you chat.

capabilities.title: Web search
capabilities.text: Look up current information when a question needs it.

helps: Claude helps you think through a problem. You can paste a long document, ask for the key points and then ask follow-up questions about the details.
It is also handy for turning rough notes into clear text, or for reviewing a draft and pointing out weak spots.
why: Many people like Claude for its clear, well-organised writing and for the way it handles large amounts of text.
Alongside the chat app, there are tools for developers, so the same assistant can fit into a coding workflow.

workflows.title: Summarise a long file
workflows.text: Upload a PDF and ask for a short summary, then for the main risks or open questions.

workflows.title: Work on a project
workflows.text: Keep instructions and reference files together so each chat starts with the right context.

workflows.title: Review code
workflows.text: Paste a function and ask for bugs, edge cases and cleaner alternatives.

workflows.title: Build a draft
workflows.text: Ask for an outline, edit it, then expand each section in turn.

beyond.purpose: Keep files and instructions together for one piece of work
Create and edit documents, code and pages beside the chat
Gather information from many sources into a report
Delegate coding tasks from the command line
Let the assistant work with websites in your browser
Build Claude into your own apps

tips: Paste the full text instead of a short excerpt when context matters.
Say what the result is for, for example an email to a client or notes for a class.
Ask it to point out what it is unsure about.
Double-check important facts and figures yourself.
Features and plan limits change often, so check the official site for current details.
audience: Claude suits writers, researchers, analysts, students and developers, especially anyone who works with long or detailed material.
It is a good choice when you want a thoughtful second pair of eyes on your work.

intro: `DeepSeek` is an AI assistant from DeepSeek, a Chinese AI company. You can chat with it for free on the web and in its app, and the company has released open-weight models that developers can download and run themselves.
It has drawn attention for strong coding and reasoning results and for making its models easy to access.

capabilities.title: Free chat
capabilities.text: Use the assistant on the web or in the app at no cost.

capabilities.title: Coding help
capabilities.text: Write, explain and debug code in many languages.

capabilities.title: Reasoning mode
capabilities.text: Work through maths and logic problems step by step.

capabilities.title: Web search option
capabilities.text: Turn on search when an answer needs recent information.

capabilities.title: Open-weight models
capabilities.text: Download models to study, test or run on your own hardware.

helps: DeepSeek helps with problems that need careful, step-by-step thinking, such as maths questions, algorithm puzzles and tricky bugs.
For developers, the open models also make it possible to experiment without relying only on a hosted service.
why: Its combination of free access, solid coding and reasoning ability, and open model releases makes it popular with students and developers.
Open weights also let researchers and companies run the models in their own environment.

workflows.title: Solve a problem
workflows.text: Switch on the reasoning mode and ask it to show its steps.

workflows.title: Code review
workflows.text: Paste a function and ask for bugs, tests and a cleaner version.

workflows.title: Learn an algorithm
workflows.text: Ask for a plain explanation, then a worked example.

workflows.title: Local experiments
workflows.text: Run a smaller open model on your own machine to test ideas privately.

beyond.purpose: Show step-by-step thinking for harder problems
Pull in recent information from the web
Download and run the models yourself
Use the models inside your own apps
Keep data on your own servers when you run a model locally

tips: State the problem clearly and include the exact error or input.
Use the reasoning mode for maths and logic, and normal chat for quick questions.
Check code and calculations before using them in real work.
Do not paste private or sensitive data into any online chatbot, and read the privacy policy first.
Features change often, so check the official site for current details.
audience: DeepSeek suits students, developers and researchers who want a capable free assistant, or open models they can run themselves.
It is also a good option for anyone comparing different AI assistants.

intro: `Gemini` is Google's AI assistant. It works with text, images, audio and video, and it connects with Google services such as Search, Gmail and Docs, and with Android phones.
You can use it on the web, in mobile apps and inside some Google products.

capabilities.title: Multimodal input
capabilities.text: Ask questions about text, pictures, audio and video in the same chat.

capabilities.title: Google integration
capabilities.text: Work with information from Google apps you choose to connect.

capabilities.title: Writing and editing
capabilities.text: Draft, rewrite and summarise text for email, documents and more.

capabilities.title: Coding help
capabilities.text: Explain, write and fix code in many languages.

capabilities.title: Live conversation
capabilities.text: Talk with the assistant by voice in a natural back-and-forth.

capabilities.title: Research
capabilities.text: Gather information from many sources into a structured report.

helps: Gemini helps most when your work already lives in Google's apps. It can help you summarise an email thread, draft a document or plan around information you have saved.
Because it understands images and audio too, you can show it a photo or a recording instead of describing it.
why: Its close link with Google Search and Workspace makes it convenient for people who use those tools every day.
It is also built into many Android phones, so help is easy to reach.

workflows.title: Plan a trip
workflows.text: Ask for ideas, compare options and turn the result into a simple itinerary.

workflows.title: Summarise your inbox
workflows.text: Connect your mail and ask for a summary of a long thread or a list of open tasks.

workflows.title: Learn from a photo
workflows.text: Upload a picture of a diagram or a page and ask for an explanation.

workflows.title: Research a topic
workflows.text: Use the research mode to collect sources into a report you can read and check.

beyond.purpose: Custom assistants with saved instructions
Spoken conversation with the assistant
Multi-step research that ends in a report
A workspace for editing documents and code
Use Gmail, Docs and other Google apps with the assistant
Let developers build with the Gemini models

tips: Connect only the apps you are comfortable sharing.
Attach the image or file instead of describing it.
Ask it to cite or point to its sources for facts you plan to use.
Verify important details before you act on them.
Features and plans change often, so check the official site for current details.
audience: Gemini suits people who use Google's apps and Android every day, as well as students, researchers and developers.
It is a natural choice if you want an assistant that sits close to your email, documents and phone.

intro: `Kimi` is an AI assistant from Moonshot AI, a company based in China. It is known for reading long documents and for research-style tasks, and it is free to use.
You can chat with it on the web and in mobile apps.

capabilities.title: Long documents
capabilities.text: Read and summarise long texts, reports and papers.

capabilities.title: Research help
capabilities.text: Gather and organise information on a topic.

capabilities.title: Writing and summaries
capabilities.text: Draft, rewrite and shorten text.

capabilities.title: Coding help
capabilities.text: Write, explain and debug code.

capabilities.title: File uploads
capabilities.text: Ask questions about documents you upload.

capabilities.title: Web search
capabilities.text: Look up fresh information when a question needs it.

helps: Kimi helps when you have a lot of reading to get through. Upload a long document, then ask for the main points or for answers to specific questions.
It is also useful for first-pass research, where you want a quick overview before reading the sources in depth.
why: People try Kimi for its strength with long inputs and for its free access.
Moonshot AI has also released open models, so developers can experiment with the technology behind it.

workflows.title: Digest a long paper
workflows.text: Upload it, ask for a summary, then ask about the method and the results.

workflows.title: Compare sources
workflows.text: Share several documents and ask where they agree and differ.

workflows.title: Prepare a report
workflows.text: Collect facts with search, then ask for an outline and a first draft.

workflows.title: Study notes
workflows.text: Turn lecture material into short notes and review questions.

beyond.purpose: Handle very long documents in one chat
Bring in current information
Ask questions about your own documents
Let developers run Moonshot's released models themselves
Build the models into your own apps

tips: Ask specific questions about a long document instead of one broad request.
Ask for page or section references so you can check the answer.
Verify key facts before using them in real work.
Avoid sharing private or sensitive files, and read the privacy policy first.
Features change often, so check the official site for current details.
audience: Kimi suits students, researchers, analysts and anyone who regularly reads long material.
It is a good one to try alongside other assistants when you want to compare how they handle large documents.

intro: `Qwen` is a family of AI models from Alibaba Cloud. Qwen Chat is the assistant you can talk to on the web, and many of the models are released with open weights.
The family covers text, images and code, in a range of sizes.

capabilities.title: Multilingual chat
capabilities.text: Work in many languages, including Chinese and English.

capabilities.title: Open-weight models
capabilities.text: Download models in different sizes to run on your own hardware.

capabilities.title: Coding models
capabilities.text: Use versions tuned to write and explain code.

capabilities.title: Image understanding
capabilities.text: Ask questions about pictures with the vision models.

capabilities.title: Web chat
capabilities.text: Try the models without installing anything.

capabilities.title: Cloud API
capabilities.text: Use the models through Alibaba Cloud in your own apps.

helps: Qwen helps you write, translate, reason and code, and it gives developers a family of models to build on.
Because there are both small and large versions, you can pick one that fits a laptop or one that needs a server.
why: Qwen is widely used by developers who want capable open models, and its strong support for several languages makes it useful beyond English.
A broad family means one project can use the same technology at different sizes and costs.

workflows.title: Translate and write
workflows.text: Draft text in one language and ask for a natural version in another.

workflows.title: Run locally
workflows.text: Download a smaller model and run it on your machine for private experiments.

workflows.title: Build an app
workflows.text: Call a hosted model through the API and add it to a product.

workflows.title: Code assistance
workflows.text: Use a coding model to write functions and explain unfamiliar code.

beyond.purpose: Choose between small and large versions
Specialised versions for programming tasks
Understand images as well as text
Download, study and fine-tune the models
Use hosted models in your own apps

tips: Start with a small model if you want to try running one locally.
Check the licence of the specific model before using it in a product.
Test results in your own language, since quality can differ by task.
Avoid sharing private data with any online service, and read the privacy policy first.
Models and features change often, so check the official site for the current list.
audience: Qwen suits developers, researchers and teams who want open models, and anyone who works across several languages.
It is also a good choice for people who want to learn how to run an AI model on their own machine.
